decision.summary: Tenant reports an intermittent chirp from a sealed-battery CO alarm fitted April 2019 (7-year life), so it is past end of life. Not treated as a CO emergency on current facts, but symptoms were not confirmed as the call dropped. Raised an urgent replacement job, sent safety advice, asked the landlord for approval, and logged the extractor fan separately.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, battery issue, or end-of-life alarm? How did you decide?
answers.answer: Most likely an end-of-life alarm. It chirps about once a minute (not continuous), the battery is sealed so it can't be a simple battery swap, and the unit was fitted 2019-04-02 with a 7-year life, so it expired around April 2026. Not an emergency unless the tenant reports symptoms or a continuous alarm. That was not confirmed because the call dropped, so the safety questions were sent by SMS.

answers.question: Who is responsible, citing the clause?
answers.answer: The landlord is responsible for replacing the expired sealed unit. Clause 12.8 (tenant replaces batteries) doesn't apply as the battery can't be replaced. Clause 12.9 means the tenant tests and reports faults, which she did. Clause 12.17 (avoidable call-out charge) doesn't apply as the report was prompt and the fault is genuine. The £300 limit should cover the replacement.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created urgent JOB-101 and routine JOB-103 (extractor fan). Requested landlord approval (APR-104) and set a follow-up for 12 Oct. Texted the tenant: don't remove the battery or disable the alarm, leave and call 0800 111 999 (999 if unwell) if it goes continuous or anyone has symptoms, please confirm everyone is well, replacement targeted within 72 hours, and she'll hear from us by Monday.

conflicts: The tenant asked to remove the battery, but the CRM shows a sealed battery. Trusted the CRM and advised against tampering.
assumptions: Chirp is the end-of-life signal given the 2019 fit date and 7-year lifespan.
Replacement cost is within the £300 limit.

Please reply to tell us: is it only chirping, and is everyone feeling well? We're arranging a replacement alarm as an urgent job (target within 72 hours) and will update you by Monday. We've also noted the noisy extractor fan as a separate routine job.
